_about: Reference vehicle for Portfolio Project 1 (FSAE-class front suspension). Own assumptions, no team data. Geometry in mm, masses in kg, everything else SI unless the key says otherwise. Keys ending _assumed are engineering assumptions stated in the write-up; sourced values cite notes/requirements.md section 8.
_public_comparison: Inside published FSAE ranges: wheelbase 1525-1684 mm, front track 1180-1439 mm, mass with driver about 215-328 kg, front share 45-50.5 %, CG 260-308 mm (TU Graz 2012-2019 cars on formulastudent.de: 1550 mm wheelbase, 10 in wheels, 46 % front; eForce FSE.11; NAU 2024 spec sheet; Ojaswat 2020). Round values chosen inside those ranges; no team data.
configuration: Aero-less baseline (no wings: the rear-wing project adds aero later); mass basis is a single-cylinder combustion car with a 68 kg driver.

tyre.vertical_stiffness_basis: Hoosier setup guideline (TTC data), 12 psi on 8 in rim: 724 lb/in at 200 lb, trend extrapolated to the 150 lb static corner load = 699 lb/in = 122 N/mm (an estimate: extrapolated)
tyre.pneumatic_trail_basis: The lateral force acts this far behind the contact patch (aligning moment = Fy x trail). Typical FSAE slicks carry 10-25 mm near the friction peak, falling towards zero at saturation, so 15 mm at the design g is a conservative middle value. Applied to the contact-patch load cases with a lateral force.

wheel.model: Braid Sturace FSAE 10 x 6 in, made to specification (rennline.com listing: 10 in and 13 in 'in any specification')
wheel.note: 6 in rather than 7 in (RC-6): the CAD interference sweep showed no wishbone geometry keeps a 7 in rim's inboard lip clear of the legs at full steering lock. Hoosier's current spec table (hoosiertire.com/tires/circuit-racing, read 2026-10-26) gives 6-8 in as the recommended rim range for the 43075, measured on 8 in; the 2018 launch table said 7-8 in, so confirm with Hoosier before ordering. The tyre data (rate, section) are measured on 8 in; on 6 in the section is narrower and the tyre a little softer (ride-frequency effect under 1 %). Mass kept at the 10x7 figure (conservative). ET 35 moves the disc outboard to clear the steering-arm rod end.

damper.bump_rubber_note: Bump rubber on the damper shaft. Travel stops where the damper length = compressed length + the rubber's solid height; that must fall between +25 mm (FSAE V.3.1.1 jounce) and +30 mm (the end of the swept envelope the clearances were checked over). Droop is limited by the damper's extended length (top-out), which must leave at least 25 mm. The BOM rubber must have a solid height in the window that kinematics.py reports.

spring_catalogue.range: Ohlins' TTX25 MkII FSAE (GTTX25) listing gives these 13 rates, 150-650 lb/in; Hyperco's Formula SAE springs for it (18FS<rate>: 1.450 in ID, 4.400 in free length) run 150-400 lb/in. 150 lb/in is the softest either sells
spring_catalogue.chosen_part: Hyperco FSAE spring, 150 lb/in: Essex 09.03.FS150 (55.00 USD, sold for the TTX25 MkII); Summit lists the same rate as HYC-18FS150
spring_catalogue.source: https://www.mlperformance.co.uk/products/ohlins-gttx25-professional-motorsport-products-ttx-25-mkii-fsae-200-57-mm (rates); https://www.summitracing.com/search/product-line/hyperco-formula-sae-coilover-springs (Hyperco line, ID and free length); https://www.essexparts.com/hyperco-fsae-coil-spring-150lbsin (part and price); read 2026-11-04. Replaces an assumed 2.5 N/mm metric list

ride_frequency_front_basis: Revised from PLAN's 3.2 Hz (requirement change RC-2): public FSAE practice for aero-less cars is about 2-3 Hz, and 2.8 Hz is what lets the 1.0 deg/g roll-gradient and 52 % TLLTD targets hold together

arb_bar.model: Solid 4340 torsion bar, heat treated to 180 ksi, splined ends; three bars set the rate (soft, middle, stiff) and the bar is swapped to adjust; two stiff 4130N levers; drop links off = disconnected (D26)
arb_bar.settings_basis: Fractions of the stiff setting's roll stiffness. The middle setting gives the TLLTD target, so the bars adjust the balance both ways from it
arb_bar.bars_basis: Body diameters sized so each bar (its body, plus the upset ends on to each hub's centre), in series with the two levers' bending, gives its setting within setting_tolerance_pct (vehicle_calcs.py checks it, S-22); rounded to 0.1 mm (the bodies are turned and ground)
arb_bar.shoulder_basis: The upset starts upset_runout_mm inboard of each lever hub; the body steps up to it with an R4 fillet (the CAD shows the step sharp). HC-5 checks the fillet in fatigue (Kt from the torsion fits), S-23
arb_bar.spline_basis: Ends upset to 25 mm and splined into the levers, spline minor diameter 23 mm (the spline is not detailed; 22 / 20 mm until step E, when the fatigue check took the 99 % reliability factor and the machined spline failed). Kt 3.0 on the minor diameter in torsion is taken at the high end of the splined-shaft range (Peterson, read second-hand); HC-5 checks the ends. Machined from 28 mm bar; the body and its R4 fillets ground
arb_bar.lever_basis: The drop link's lever-end rod end is bolted through the lever along the bar's axis, beside it on a 5 mm misalignment spacer, with a second spacer and a 24 mm washer outside it (single shear, captured; D25). So the lever's mid-plane sits 15 mm inboard of the ball centre ARB_L (6 mm half ball + 5 mm spacer + 4 mm half lever), and the bar's free length between the lever hubs is 2 x (|ARB_P y| - 15). 8 x 25 mm (D26): strong enough at the warp torque (S-21) and much stiffer than the stiff bar (S-08); the 6 x 18 mm placeholder of D25 reached FoS 0.95
arb_bar.note: History: v1.0-v1.5 a 3/4 x 0.049 in tube in series with adjustable blades (only 1.24x the stiff-blade requirement); v1.6 1.0 x 0.049 in (FoS 1.28 in warp, second Week 2 audit); v1.7 1.0 x 0.065 in. Step D (D26): blades dropped. A blade rotated to adjust turns the through-bolted rod end past its rating (D25), and a blade compliant enough to set the rate would see about 1500 MPa at the warp torque, so the rate moves into a solid bar and the levers are made stiff

steering.note: Steering-effort case LC6 (abuse case): the driver pulls 25 N m on the STEERING wheel with the road wheels blocked (kerb or stop); the whole rack force then loads one tie rod. 25 N m is an assumed hard pull, not a cited value.

load_cases.name: 3 g bump (3 x static corner load)
1.2 g braking + 1.2 g cornering, outside wheel (envelope: about 10 % beyond the friction ellipse)
pothole edge strike: 3 x static corner load at 45 deg, through the wheel centre, brakes off
kerb strike: 2.5 x static corner load inboard on the outer sidewall, 100 mm up, plus static weight

caliper.model: Wilwood PS-1 (120-5453 RH / 120-5456 LH), 2 x 1.00 in pistons, lug mount
caliper.note: Chosen because it is the only FSAE-class caliper with a fully dimensioned public drawing. Its bridge sits 23.9 mm beyond the disc edge, so the disc is 180 mm (not 190) to keep the bridge 7 mm inside the rim barrel. Pad effective radius = disc radius - 13 mm (half the pad height, estimated).
caliper.piston_basis: PS-1: two 1.00 in pistons, one each side (Wilwood's page); the line pressure for a pad clamp force is force / one piston's area

hub.bearings: SKF 32008 X tapered roller pair, back-to-back (O arrangement), 40 x 68 x 19 mm; preload set by a cone spacer ground (or shimmed) to the measured bearing standout, the axle nut torqued to clamp the stack
hub.source: RS Components SKF 32008 X https://uk.rs-online.com/web/p/roller-bearings/0506769 and Acorn 32008-X-XL https://www.acorn-ind.co.uk/p/fag/single-row-tapered-roller-bearings/32008-x-xl-fag (C0 71 kN, C 64.7 kN, 0.28 kg; read 2026-10-26). Y0 0.9 is a conservative value for this series (confirm with the SKF datasheet). Pressure-centre offset from the bearing centre about (d + D) / 4 x tan(14 deg) = 6.7 mm, outward for a back-to-back pair (geometric estimate). Cup width C = 14.5 mm (the overall width T = 19 mm includes the cone and rollers standing proud of the cup); the cups sit against the central rib, so each is loaded over the 14.5 mm next to the rib.
hub.history: Layout (v1.0-v1.7): SKF 71908 CD angular contact pair (C0 8.5 kN each) at 24 mm centres. upright_loads.py showed 9-12 kN per row in LC2 and LC4, s0 0.69-0.76: overloaded. A 7009 CD pair (C0 22.4 kN) would give about 1.9; the tapered pair gives about 5.
hub.note: Axial positions from the wheel centre plane, + outboard. Two 19 mm cones back to back on a ground spacer; the two 14.5 mm cups pressed against a 2 mm central rib in the upright bore.
hub.C_basis: Distributors list 60-64.7 kN for the 32008 X; the lowest (60) is used.
hub.factors_basis: Contact angle 14.2 deg (klium.be listing of SKF 32008 X/Q); e = 1.5 tan a, Y = 0.4 cot a, Y0 = 0.22 cot a (ISO 76 / ISO 281 formulas for tapered roller bearings).

fits.housing: P6 on the 68 mm cup seats (13-45 um interference at 20 C), plus a bearing-retaining compound (Loctite 641)
fits.shaft: m6 on the 40 mm hub spindle (rotating inner-ring load)
fits.retention: cups pressed in from each side against a central rib in the upright bore (back-to-back pair: both cups are loaded towards the centre); cones clamped by the axle nut, which sets a light preload

duty.spectrum_basis: Assumed share of distance in each load state for an aero-less FSAE car over testing, autocross and endurance; inside / outside wheel split evenly. Edit to match logged data when available.

cycle_model.basis: Events per km for a tight FSAE autocross / endurance course (about 20 direction changes and 8 braking zones per km; 10 bumps or kerb strikes at 2 g). Corner events are shared among the cornering states (including braking-while-cornering) by their distance share, brake events among the braking states, and every corner is counted as a full outside-to-inside reversal (a slalom), which is conservative: a corner followed by a straight is a smaller cycle. Brake and bump events cycle against the 1 g static state.
